spec_match.rationale: Implements the spec's own example verbatim (a:navigation-source .thumb { view-transition-name: active-image }) against a hero carrying the same name, driven by real navigations — the exact motivation ChromeStatus cites for shipping the feature.

interactive.rationale: Four navigable cards, a real same-document navigation per click, a real view transition morphing thumb→hero, a back link that is itself a navigation source, and a narrated readout.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index card promises the thumbnail-morph use case run live with a labelled JS mirror; that is what the page does.

edge_cases.rationale: Handles prefers-reduced-motion (skips the transition, records it), missing startViewTransition, missing Navigation API (click-target stand-in, explicitly labelled), deep links/reload via hash routing, and traversals routed through the same handler.

references.rationale: Links chromestatus.com/feature/6327898878377984, the spec anchor, and the route-matching explainer's link-matching section.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite's spec-example-compound-parses assertion pins the exact selector this page relies on; suite runs cleanly on the conformance route.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Scripted headless Chromium 141 at both viewports: clicking the Ember card swapped to the hero (gallery hidden, title updated, focus moved to the back link), the readout named the source card and honestly reported the native probe's SyntaxError, the back link returned to the gallery, and no simulation class leaked after settle; zero page overflow, console clean. chrome-devtools-mcp unavailable; the native-tagging branch (no JS mirror needed) requires Chrome 156+.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts stage-armed, hero-swap-completed per navigation with print id and source, reduced-motion-respected, and nav-api-missing-fallback on the degraded branch.

design_system.rationale: Thumbnails are CSS-variable gradients (no raw hex), focus-visible enhancement on cards, back link ≥44px, all copy on AA-compliant pairs.

accessibility.rationale: Cards are real links in a labelled nav; the readout is role=status aria-live=polite; focus moves to the back link when the hero opens (verified: activeElement was back-link); decorative thumbs are aria-hidden with the card title carrying the accessible name; reduced-motion preference disables the animation.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Verified at 360×740 DPR3 touch and 1280×800: gallery reflows via auto-fill minmax, hero and transition behave identically, scrollWidth 360 with the code sample scrolling inside its pre.

openQuestions.title: Verify the native no-JS morph on Chrome 156+
openQuestions.detail: On a supporting build the JS mirror becomes redundant: a:navigation-source .thumb should tag the clicked thumbnail natively before the transition snapshot. Verify on Chrome Canary ≥156 that disabling the mirror (temporarily, in DevTools) still yields the morph, and consider surfacing 'native tagging active' in the readout when CSS.supports reports true.

openQuestions.title: Add a cross-document variant when a second demo origin/page is justified
openQuestions.detail: The explainer's headline scenario is cross-document MPA transitions with @view-transition { navigation: auto }. A future additive concept could pair two sibling documents under this feature folder to demonstrate the outgoing page's :navigation-source during a real cross-document navigation on a supporting build — additive slug, not a rewrite of this page.

guidanceConsulted.query: styling in-progress navigations and cross-document view transitions
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Gate view-transition animations behind prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference and let the browser pair old/new elements via view-transition-name.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: startViewTransition is skipped (with a telemetry record) when reduced motion is preferred; the morph is driven purely by matching view-transition-name values, with the pseudo-class/mirror supplying the old-state name.

guidanceConsulted.query: styling in-progress navigations and cross-document view transitions
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: For SPA-style morphs, set the shared view-transition-name on the source before the DOM swap inside startViewTransition.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The mirror class (and natively the pseudo-class, which starts matching at the navigate event) is applied before startViewTransition captures the old state — the exact race the feature eliminates, called out in the page copy.

summary: The motivating use case, working today through real navigations and real view transitions, with the pseudo-class's contribution mirrored and clearly labelled as simulation until 156. Interaction, focus management, reduced-motion, both viewports and clean console verified on Chromium 141.
